'''Gerhard Frey''' ({{IPA|de|fʁaɪ|lang}}; born 1 June 1944) is a German mathematician, known for his work in [[number theory]]. Following an original idea of {{ill|Yves Hellegouarch|fr|lt=Hellegouarch}},<ref>{{Citation | last1=Hellegouarch | first1=Yves | title=Points d'ordre 2p<sup>h</sup> sur les courbes elliptiques | url=http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa26/aa2636.pdf| mr=0379507  | year=1975 | journal=Polska Akademia Nauk. Instytut Matematyczny. Acta Arithmetica | issn=0065-1036 | volume=26 | issue=3 | pages=253–263| doi=10.4064/aa-26-3-253-263 }}</ref> he developed the notion of [[Frey–Hellegouarch curve|Frey–Hellegouarch curves]], a construction of an [[elliptic curve]] from a purported solution to the [[Fermat's Last Theorem|Fermat equation]], that is central to [[Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem]].<ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/are-mathematicians-finall/ | title= Are mathematicians finally satisfied with Andrew Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem? Why has this theorem been so difficult to prove? | author=Helen G. Grundman | date= 21 October 1999 | publisher= Scientific American | access-date=21 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/1999/jul/21/technology | title=Beyond Fermat's last theorem | author=Keith Devlin | date=21 July 1999 | work=[[The Guardian]] | access-date=21 August 2016}}</ref>

==Education and career==
He studied mathematics and [[physics]] at the [[University of Tübingen]], graduating in 1967. He continued his postgraduate studies at [[Heidelberg University]], where he received his PhD in 1970,<ref>{{MathGenealogy|29309}}</ref> and his [[Habilitation]] in 1973. He was assistant professor at Heidelberg University from 1969–1973, professor at the [[University of Erlangen-Nuremberg|University of Erlangen]] (1973–1975) and at [[Saarland University]] (1975–1990). Until 2009, he held a chair for [[number theory]] at the Institute for Experimental Mathematics at the [[University of Duisburg-Essen]], campus [[Essen]].

Frey was a visiting scientist at several universities and research institutions, including the [[Ohio State University]], [[Harvard University]], the [[University of California, Berkeley]], the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] (MSRI), the Institute for Advanced Studies at [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], and the [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada]] (IMPA) in [[Rio de Janeiro]].

Frey was also the co-editor of the journal ''{{ill|Manuscripta Mathematica|fr||nl}}''.

==Research contributions==
[[File:Gerhard Frey, Boston 1995.JPG|upright|thumb|Frey at a convention in Boston, 1995]]
His research areas are [[number theory]] and [[diophantine geometry]], as well as applications to [[coding theory]] and [[cryptography]]. 
In 1985, Frey pointed out a connection between [[Fermat's Last Theorem]] and the [[Taniyama-Shimura conjecture]], and this connection was made precise shortly thereafter by [[Jean-Pierre Serre]], who formulated the [[Ribet's theorem|epsilon conjecture]], and showed that the Taniyama-Shimura and epsilon conjectures together imply Fermat. Soon after, [[Ken Ribet]] proved enough of the epsilon conjecture to deduce that Taniyama-Shimura implied Fermat's Last Theorem.<ref>{{cite book |first=Piergiorgio |last=Odifreddi |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zAIar8Ee80QC&pg=PA86 |title=The Mathematical Century: The 30 Greatest Problems of the Last 100 years |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |year=2006 |isbn=0-691-12805-7 |page=87 }}</ref> This approach provided a framework for the subsequent successful attack on Fermat's Last Theorem by [[Andrew Wiles]] in the 1990s.<ref>{{cite news |first=Richard |last=Bernstein |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/11/28/books/books-times-following-proof-fermat-s-theorem-far-horizon-pure-reason.html?pagewanted=1 |title=Following a Proof of Fermat's Theorem to the Far Horizon of Pure Reason |newspaper=[[New York Times]] |date=November 28, 1997 |access-date=January 24, 2010 }}</ref>

In 1998, Frey proposed the idea of [[Weil descent]] attack for elliptic curves over finite fields with composite degree. As a result of this attack, [[Cryptography|cryptographers]] lost their interest in these curves.<ref>{{citation|title=Guide to Elliptic Curve Cryptography|first1=Darrel|last1=Hankerson|first2=Scott|last2=Vanstone|first3=Alfred J.|last3=Menezes|publisher=Springer|year=2004|isbn=9780387952734|pages=170–171}}.</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Frey was awarded the Gauss medal of the ''Braunschweigische Wissenschaftliche Gesellschaft'' in 1996 for his work on [[Fermat's Last Theorem]].<ref>[http://www.bwg-niedersachsen.de/cgi-bin/moin.cgi/_dcber_20die_20BWG/Die_20Gauss_20Medaille?action=highlight&value=Frey Die Gauß Medaille]{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} (in German), Braunschweigische Wissenschaftliche Gesellschaft. Accessed January 24, 2010</ref> Since 1998, he has been a member of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uni-goettingen.de/de/document/download/3716a19481c54eb4f7ff7c65c6429712.pdf/kompetenzhandbuch_web2.pdf |title=Member list |language=German |work=[[Göttingen Academy of Sciences]] |access-date=January 24, 2010 }}</ref>

In 2006, he received the ''Certicom ECC Visionary Award'' for his contributions to [[elliptic-curve cryptography]].<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://www.securitytechnet.com/resource/crypto/code&cipher/CC-06-final.pdf |title=Certicom ECC Visionary Award |journal=Code and Cipher |volume=3 |year=2006 |issue=1 |page=1 |access-date=January 24, 2010 }}{{Dead link|date=April 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
